chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Regarding the heart, when it shakes and is damaged, is the (complete) wergild (blood money).

And Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Regarding the contortion (of the neck), is the (complete) wergild; and the contortion is that his neck is bent and it comes to be on its side.
ai.seo_question: What injuries obligate the complete wergild (diyah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, establishes the legal principle that specific structural injuries to the heart and neck incur the complete wergild (diyah al-kamilah). It highlights the Prophetic tradition's precise anatomical definitions, such as 'sa'ar' (neck contortion), demonstrating the early development of forensic jurisprudence in Shia fiqh. The narration underscores the high value placed on vital organs in Islamic compensation law, linking physical integrity to spiritual and legal wholeness.
